Collective Worship
Collective worship takes place daily at Freegrounds Junior School - either in class, year groups or as a whole school.
Typically, we follow the following timetable:
'No Outsiders' Assembly
Celebration Assembly
Our Monday 'themed' assembly follows a long-term plan. Each half term, we hold assemblies related to the following:
Our Tuesday 'No Outsiders' assembly centres around a picture stimulus which children discuss. The pictures are from real-life stories which demonstrate positive stories of community cohesion, acts of kindness, empathy, hope, acceptance and confidence in a world filled with diversity and difference. These pictures are shared on our social media channels as a discussion point for families at home.
Our Thursday 'Year Group Assemblies' always include our Trickbox 'Trick of the Week' which is also shared with families at home via our social media channels.
On Fridays, we ensure we hold a weekly Celebration collective worship to recognise the achievements and efforts of our children and reflect on our School Values.

Vision and Values
At Freegrounds Junior School our vision is for the following to be true for all members of our school:
We are passionate that this ambition, which is built on a culture of high expectation, a ‘can do’ approach and positive relationships, underpins all that we do and informs the decisions that we make.
The school has a clear vision for every pupil to achieve their best.
By creating a safe, inspirational learning environment where everyone is respected and experiences success, we believe that we will enable our children to enter the next phase of their life as happy, confident and respectful citizens who are curious and have a passion for life-long learning.
Our aim is for all children to leave Freegrounds Junior School having a strong sense of pride and self-worth, being well-equipped to thrive in an ever-changing world.

SMSC/British Values

Welcome
On behalf of our entire school team, I would like to welcome you to Freegrounds Junior School.
We are a friendly community who work closely with the other schools in the Wildern Partnership, particularly Freegrounds Infant School, where the majority of our pupils join us from.
We recognise the individuality of all our pupils and aspire for them to be happy, engaged learners. It is our aim that when children leave us they will be respectful, curious, confident, successful and aspirational. These are the school’s core values and they underpin the vision and purpose of what we do.
Our curriculum is designed to enthuse and inspire children so that they are keen to increase their knowledge and understanding of the world around them. In addition, we also celebrate and develop our pupils’ skills as learners, such as their resilience or ability to think creatively, so that they are fully equipped to tackle any of the learning challenges that lie ahead of them.
We hope that you find the website a useful source of information. If you are interested in visiting our school, please contact the office who can arrange a time for you to do so.
Pupils are happy, feel safe and say that all adults are kind. The school's values of aspire, believe and achieve are ingrained throughout the school. Pupils rise to the challenges set. They work hard in their lessons and listen well.

Our School

Maths
Intent
The National Curriculum for Maths aims to ensure that all children become fluent in the fundamentals of maths, are able to reason mathematically and can solve problems by applying their mathematical skills. At Freegrounds Junior School, we aspire to embed these skills throughout maths lessons and learning journeys, and develop them consistently over time. We believe it is important to equip our pupils with a range of strategies to enable them to explain, reason and problem solve resiliently. Through appropriate challenge within lessons and additional opportunities outside of daily maths lessons, we aim for all children to master the mathematics curriculum as well as develop an enjoyment for the subject.
Implementation
At Freegrounds Junior School we follow a mastery approach to mathematics using the White Rose Schemes of Learning. Teachers use and adapt the schemes to meet the needs of the pupils in their class. The Schemes of Learning make sure topics are introduced to children in a logical order and are revisited throughout the year making links between domains to encourage deep learning and ensure children have the foundational knowledge they need, before moving on to more advanced maths concepts and tackling more challenging number problems. Through breaking the learning down into small steps, pupils develop mathematical fluency, reasoning skills and problem-solving throughout each learning journey. The use of multi-representations, concrete resources and sentence stems further support and enhance mathematical learning across all year groups and ability levels.

Within a mixed ability class, groupings are flexible in order to meet the needs of each pupil. Through the use of working walls and checking stations, children are encouraged to develop independence in their learning. Class teachers consistently use formative assessment techniques and summative assessments in order to appropriately support and challenge each pupil.
All pupils have logins to TT Rockstars in order to practise their multiplication tables at home, and as a school, we regularly promote special mathematical events such as: NSPCC Number Day and Barvember.
